answer: Draw grading juries so no two jurors share an anchor, meaning the established account that first funded or vouched for them. Picture the trust graph with each key as a vertex; before a panel is sealed, the sampler traces each juror back to its anchor and drops duplicates. A farmer with a thousand keys hanging off one anchor still lands at most one juror per panel, so a rigged verdict can't ripple through the jury, and every fresh anchor costs real earned reputation.
